title: A week without a phone
summary: After his phone breaks, Dani has to get through seven days the old-fashioned way.
paragraphs: Dani dropped his phone in the swimming pool on a Saturday afternoon. He pulled it out in two seconds, but it was too late. The screen stayed black. The repair shop said it would take a week to get a new part.

The first day was {{terrible}}. Dani kept putting his hand in his pocket to check for messages that could not arrive. He didn't know what time it was, because he never wore a watch. He couldn't listen to music on the bus, so he looked out of the window instead and noticed a small bookshop he had passed hundreds of times without seeing.

On Tuesday he had to meet his friend Sara at the cinema. Normally they would send twenty messages: "Where are you?", "I'm late!", "Which door?". This time they had agreed on everything the day before: seven o'clock, under the big clock, no excuses. Dani arrived at five to seven, and Sara arrived at exactly seven. "That was {{strangely}} easy," she said.

By Thursday something had changed. Dani was sleeping better, because he wasn't reading videos in bed until one in the morning. He finished a book from the little bookshop. He called his grandmother from the phone at home, and they talked for forty minutes. She sounded {{surprised}} and very happy.

When the repair shop called to say the phone was ready, Dani felt almost {{disappointed}}. He picked it up, of course. But he turned off most of the notifications, and now he leaves the phone in the kitchen when he goes to bed. On Fridays, he and Sara still meet under the big clock without sending a single message.

strangely.meaning: in a way that is surprising or difficult to explain

surprised.meaning: feeling that something unexpected has happened

disappointed.meaning: a little sad because something was not what you wanted

questions.question: Why was Dani without a phone for a week?
options: He lost it on the bus.
It fell into a swimming pool and needed a new part.
He decided to stop using it.
questions.explanation: He dropped it in the pool, and the repair shop needed a week to get a new part.

questions.question: What did Dani notice on the bus?
options: A bookshop he had never seen before
questions.explanation: He looked out of the window and noticed a small bookshop he had passed many times.

questions.question: Why was meeting Sara easy?
options: They had agreed the time and place the day before.
questions.explanation: They agreed on everything the day before: seven o'clock, under the big clock.

questions.question: What did Dani change after he got his phone back?
options: He turned off most notifications and leaves it in the kitchen at night.
He only uses it to call his grandmother.
questions.explanation: He turned off most notifications and leaves the phone in the kitchen when he goes to bed.
